{"pagination":{"count":10,"page":1,"next_page":2,"total_count":1000,"total_pages":100},"records":[{"id":10994,"platform":"ios","screens_count":5,"refero_url":"https://refero.design/flows/10994","name":"Daily Journal Entry with Photo Attachment","description":"Happy path: A user creates or edits a daily journal entry, types freeform text, taps the image icon to attach a single photo, grants or confirms photo-library access, selects an image from the system photo picker, and then saves the entry using the Done button. Entry point: journal entry editor (text field with keyboard visible). Exit point: editor closed after tapping Done (entry saved). Assumptions: user is on an iPhone-like device, is editing or creating a single-day journal entry, the app triggers the system photo-permission dialog and system photo picker (iOS-style), and the app supports attaching one image to an entry.","problem":"User task: Attach a photo to a daily text entry and save the entry. From the user's perspective they want to continue writing, add a single illustrative photo from their device, and finish by saving. Decisions include whether to grant photo access, which image to choose, and when to finish editing. They expect the photo picker to appear after tapping the image icon, to be able to select one image, to see that image attached to their entry, and to persist the entry when they tap Done.

Interface/system perspective: The UI provides a text-edit area with an image-attachment control and a prominent Done action. Tapping the image icon invokes the operating system photo-permission dialog (if needed) and then opens the system photo picker configured to allow a single selection. After the user selects an image, the UI renders a preview of the selected image within the editor and keeps the keyboard available for further editing. Tapping Done signals the app to persist changes and dismiss the editor.

Result at the end:
- User-perceived outcome: The journal entry contains the typed text and the selected image; the user returns to the previous context (editor closed).
- System-level outcome: The app receives photo-library access or selection, stores a reference (or copy) of the chosen image attached to the entry, and persists the updated entry when Done is tapped.","steps":["Compose journal entry","Photo library permission prompt","Choose one image","Preview attached image in editor","Save and exit editor"],"app":{"id":268,"name":"one year","description":"capture one memory every day","background_url":"https://images.refero.design/backgrounds/app_268/aa7afef3-2fc1-4122-a4df-3ce6f5f76145.jpg","refero_url":"https://refero.design/apps/268","categories":["Health & Wellness"],"icon_url":"https://images.refero.design/favicon/app_268/dcc9e5ac-0c2c-4809-a47e-c09485c88d4c.jpg","background_color":"81a0fe"}},{"id":10993,"platform":"ios","screens_count":9,"refero_url":"https://refero.design/flows/10993","name":"Create daily memory with photo","description":"Happy path for creating a daily memory/entry and attaching a photo. Entry point: daily timeline view for a specific date with category icons across the top. When there are no saved memories the screen shows an empty state with a prominent + control to add a memory. User taps +, types a text entry, optionally taps the image icon to attach a photo (system photo-permission prompt -> photo grid -> choose image). User finishes by tapping Done which saves the entry and returns to the dated timeline where the new memory is shown as a card (thumbnail + text). The user can tap the attached image to view it fullscreen. Assumptions: user is on a mobile device, not initially granted photo access, and is interacting while viewing a single date/category.","problem":"User task (user perspective): Create and save a daily memory/reflection for a selected date and category, optionally attach a photo from the device, and review the saved memory. The user expects a simple write flow with an easy way to add an image, clear permission handling if photo access is required, and confirmation that the entry was saved and can be viewed. Interface perspective: The UI provides a date/category selector, an empty-state CTA to add a memory, a minimal writing surface with a visible image attachment icon and a Done action. If photo access is needed the app displays the system permission dialog, then a photo picker grid. After selecting an image the picker closes, a thumbnail card appears above the text editor, and tapping Done stores the memory and returns to the date view. Outcome: User-perceived outcome — a new memory card appears on the selected date with text and an attached image; system-level outcome — the entry is persisted (saved) and the app has either requested (or been granted) photo-library access to allow selection.","steps":["Date timeline / empty state","New entry editor (initial)","Typing text","Text completed / image attachment intent","Photo permission modal","Photo grid picker","Image attached in editor","Saved memory in date view","Fullscreen image preview"],"app":{"id":268,"name":"one year","description":"capture one memory every day","background_url":"https://images.refero.design/backgrounds/app_268/aa7afef3-2fc1-4122-a4df-3ce6f5f76145.jpg","refero_url":"https://refero.design/apps/268","categories":["Health & Wellness"],"icon_url":"https://images.refero.design/favicon/app_268/dcc9e5ac-0c2c-4809-a47e-c09485c88d4c.jpg","background_color":"81a0fe"}},{"id":14122,"platform":"ios","screens_count":3,"refero_url":"https://refero.design/flows/14122","name":"Add Record Photo","description":"The user starts on a new record screen without an image, chooses to add a photo, captures an image using the camera, and returns to the record with the photo attached. The system also displays a FOOD tag after the image is added. The user can then review the record details and save it. The entry point is the new record editor; the exit point is the Save action. The screenshots imply an iOS mobile device, with camera access available and the user already able to create or edit the record. No authentication or permission state is shown.","problem":"The user is trying to add a visual reference to a new record, review the resulting entry, and save it. From the user’s perspective, they need to decide whether to add a photo, capture the desired subject, verify that the image and automatically displayed category are correct, and then save the record. From the interface perspective, the system provides an empty photo area, opens a camera capture surface, supports canceling or taking a photo, attaches the captured image to the record, and returns the user to the editor with the record metadata, category, amount, rating, note, and Save action visible. The user ends with a record containing the captured food photo and a FOOD tag. At the system level, the image is associated with record #0001 and the record is ready to be persisted when Save is selected; the screenshots do not show the final saved confirmation.","steps":["New Record Editor","Camera Capture","Review and Save"],"app":{"id":312,"name":"Cashcaded","description":"Expense tracker & gallery","background_url":"https://images.refero.design/backgrounds/app_312/d7cf314b-d367-40b5-a27e-abcebd93e67c.jpg","refero_url":"https://refero.design/apps/312","categories":["Finance"],"icon_url":"https://images.refero.design/favicon/app_312/d681ec36-8015-4095-9ce0-156f09e51173.jpg","background_color":"91b620"}},{"id":7990,"platform":"ios","screens_count":7,"refero_url":"https://refero.design/flows/7990","name":"Attach Photos to Journal Entry","description":"Happy path: A user is editing a journal/reflection entry and chooses to attach photos/videos. From the entry screen they tap the Add media area, open a media chooser modal, browse the photo grid, select one or more items (up to the allowed limit), confirm selection, wait for upload/processing, and then return to the journal where the selected media is shown as attached. Entry point: journal entry edit screen (written text visible). Exit point: journal edit screen with media attached. Assumptions: user is on a mobile device (iPhone status bar visible), is editing an existing entry, has granted photo library permissions, and the app supports selecting multiple items (limit visible as “Select up to 9 items”).","problem":"User task: Attach one or more photos/videos to a written journal entry so the memory is richer and can include visual context.
- From the user's perspective: They want a quick way to pick relevant images from their library, confirm selection, and see a clear indication that media has been attached. They expect to browse thumbnails, select multiple items, see a selection count/summary, and receive feedback while media uploads are processed.
- From the interface/system perspective: The UI must provide an entry point (“Add media”), open a media chooser modal, present a grid of photos with selection affordances, enforce selection limits, surface a clear CTA to confirm (Add/Done), show intermediate upload/processing states, and finally show added thumbnails in the entry. The UI also optionally includes a location indicator for selected items.
Result at the end:
- User-perceived outcome: The user sees thumbnails of the chosen photos attached to the journal entry and receives a success confirmation (e.g., “Media added” or “Done”). The entry remains editable and the top-level Done is available to finish editing.
- System-level outcome: The selected media files are queued/processed/uploaded and persisted with the journal entry; metadata (e.g., location included) is recorded and the entry’s state updates to include the attached assets.","steps":["Entry - Add media affordance","Media chooser - Intro modal","Photo grid - browse library","Photo grid - select items","Selection -> modal back","Attachment preview - confirm done","Entry screen - media attached"],"app":{"id":229,"name":"ABY Journal","description":"Private Diary, Voice Journal","background_url":"https://images.refero.design/backgrounds/app_229/343870cc-9f56-43d6-81a4-154b8348717a.jpg","refero_url":"https://refero.design/apps/229","categories":["Health & Wellness","AI Tool","Lifestyle"],"icon_url":"https://images.refero.design/favicon/app_229/57d6e61f-5bd6-4b4b-8eec-dd68f5b5d7c9.jpg","background_color":"2fafee"}},{"id":6331,"platform":"ios","screens_count":23,"refero_url":"https://refero.design/flows/6331","name":"Create journal entry with mood, people and tags","description":"Happy path: user opens the app onboarding, selects a mood, creates a journal entry by adding text, time, people and tags, confirms the entry, optionally adds a new person (with avatar/name) and grants notifications. Entry is saved and appears on the Journal timeline. Entry point: app welcome screen. Exit point: Journal timeline showing the newly created entry. Assumptions: user is on a mobile device, first-time run for this account (onboarding shown), user has permission to open system pickers (date/time) and camera/photos for adding pictures.","problem":"Task: Record a quick mood + short journal entry and annotate it with time, people and tags so it appears on the user's timeline.

User perspective:
- Goal: capture how they feel and what they did (short text), add relevant context (who they were with, good/bad tags), optionally set the exact time, and save the entry quickly.
- Decisions: pick a mood (very good → very bad), optionally edit time, add people, pick tags from 'Good Stuff' or 'Oh Boy...' lists, then confirm the entry.
- Expectations: tapping options immediately updates the entry preview; a final confirm saves the entry and returns them to the journal timeline.

Interface/system perspective:
- The UI guides flow: onboarding → mood selection → entry form. Mood selection sets the mood state. The entry form exposes: time (editable via an ellipsis menu), a free-text field (tapping opens keyboard), People (plus button opens a modal to add/select person), Tag groups (chips representing tags, toggle selection state), and two persistent action controls: a mood pill and a save/confirm button.
- System behaviors: tapping ellipsis reveals time-edit option; time-edit uses a modal picker and updates the displayed time; the People modal supports avatar selection or choosing a picture and entering a name; tag chips toggle between unselected (light) and selected (dark) states; tapping the confirm/check button saves the entry and shows a completion screen; the app then requests system notification permission.

Result at end:
- User-perceived outcome: a confirmation screen ('First entry done') followed by the Journal showing the new entry in the Afternoon slot with mood, text, people chips and selected tags visible.
- System-level outcome: a persisted journal entry record created with fields: mood, timestamp, text, people (array with avatar/name), selected tags; UI updated to show the entry on the timeline and notification permission requested.","steps":["Welcome / Intro","Mood selection","Entry form (initial)","Time edit menu","Time picker","Text input (keyboard open)","Type entry","Open People add modal","Choose avatar / picture","Enter person name","Add second person","Select 'Good Stuff' tags","Select 'Oh Boy...' tags","Confirm mood / save entry","Success / Onboarding completion","Notification permission prompt","Journal timeline - entry listed","Entry expanded view on timeline","Edit tags later (implicit)","End state - Journal overview"],"app":{"id":200,"name":"UNHINGED","description":"Easy Mood Tracker & Journal","background_url":"https://images.refero.design/backgrounds/app_200/1946e1ee-dafd-45ba-9599-e60487b92708.jpg","refero_url":"https://refero.design/apps/200","categories":["Health & Wellness"],"icon_url":"https://images.refero.design/favicon/app_200/c168e999-a494-413e-b5b7-7b9705799ba3.jpg","background_color":"b7b715"}},{"id":7157,"platform":"ios","screens_count":5,"refero_url":"https://refero.design/flows/7157","name":"Add Photos to Workout Entry","description":"Happy path for attaching photos to a workout entry and saving the updated entry. Entry point: user is on a workout detail/edit screen for a specific date (Saturday, Aug 16, 2025) with an empty image placeholder. The user taps the image placeholder, chooses a photo source, selects up to four photos from the device library, confirms selection, and returns to the workout detail screen where selected photos appear as thumbnails. Exit point: user finishes editing and taps Done to close/save the screen. Assumes the user is signed in and has permission to access photos/camera on their device.","problem":"User task (user perspective): The user wants to add photos to a workout entry (visuals for the workout), optionally add a caption and private notes, and save the updated workout entry. They expect to be able to choose between taking a new photo or picking from their photo library, select multiple images, preview/remove any chosen images, add text, and then complete the update.

Interface/system perspective: The UI provides an editable workout detail view with a tappable image placeholder. Tapping triggers a source chooser (take photo / camera roll). Choosing camera roll opens the system photo picker where the user can browse and multi-select photos (up to a limit). The picker shows selection state and a summary/count in the picker footer. After confirmation the selected photos are inserted as thumbnails into the workout detail header with a remove (X) affordance per thumbnail. The Done control at the bottom closes/saves the edit screen.

End result:
- User-perceived outcome: Selected photos are attached to the workout entry and visible as thumbnails; the user can add captions or private notes and then complete the edit by tapping Done.
- System-level outcome: The workout record is updated with references to the chosen photos (and any text fields edited). The photos are persisted/linked to that workout entry and selection state is cleared from the picker.","steps":["Workout detail (empty image)","Choose photo source","Browse photo library","Confirm selections","Review inserted thumbnails and finish"],"app":{"id":211,"name":"Train Fitness","description":"Auto-tracking for Apple Watch","background_url":"https://images.refero.design/backgrounds/app_211/425886e8-f7ec-4975-b27f-350fe8147f33.jpg","refero_url":"https://refero.design/apps/211","categories":["Health & Wellness","Social Networking"],"icon_url":"https://images.refero.design/favicon/app_211/234d8366-a951-4a60-8d62-b8696691b339.jpg","background_color":"d3a417"}},{"id":13959,"platform":"ios","screens_count":9,"refero_url":"https://refero.design/flows/13959","name":"Photo Memory Annotation","description":"The user opens a dated photo entry, enters editing mode, adds a text caption, changes its typography, draws a handwritten annotation over the image, and confirms the edits. The updated entry is then shown in the journal gallery. The flow starts with an existing photo entry and ends with the edited card visible among other saved entries. The screenshots show a mobile device and do not indicate an account or permission requirement.","problem":"The user wants to personalize an existing photo memory by adding a caption, choosing a visual text style, and drawing directly on the image. From the user’s perspective, they review the photo, decide what text to add, enter “Morning Time,” select a type treatment, and add freehand marks. From the interface perspective, the system provides an entry viewer, an edit mode with undo and redo controls, a text insertion target, an on-screen keyboard, typography choices, and a drawing tool. Confirming the edit saves the combined image, caption, and drawing as part of the photo entry. The user sees the finished annotated memory, while the system updates the saved card and displays it in the collection.","steps":["Photo Entry Viewer","Edit Mode","Add Caption","Caption Entry","Caption Review","Text Style Selection","Freehand Annotation","Save Edited Entry","Journal Gallery"],"app":{"id":310,"name":"pico cam","description":"Tiny camera, photo magic","background_url":"https://images.refero.design/backgrounds/app_310/4901564f-1a60-4859-87b2-3471b4229499.jpg","refero_url":"https://refero.design/apps/310","categories":["Utility"],"icon_url":"https://images.refero.design/favicon/app_310/5e4cf977-238e-4649-8d95-b817c35c8b7a.jpg","background_color":""}},{"id":12807,"platform":"ios","screens_count":5,"refero_url":"https://refero.design/flows/12807","name":"Add Photo to Playground","description":"Happy path for creating an image in the Playground editor using a photo as input. Entry begins on the main Playground canvas with style set to Animation and suggestion chips visible. The user can add a source image from their library or camera, grant camera access if needed, browse photos/collections, select an image, and return to the editor where the chosen image is attached to the prompt area. The flow ends back on the Playground canvas ready for further prompt editing or saving. Assumes the user is already in the Playground experience on a mobile device and may need camera permission to capture a new source image.","problem":"The user is trying to create or modify an image by supplying a visual source rather than typing only text. From the user’s perspective, they want to pick a suggested idea, choose an existing photo, or take a new one so the generator has input to work from. From the interface perspective, the screen provides a prompt entry field, suggested topics, and an image-source control that opens either photo library browsing or camera capture. If camera access is required, the system interrupts with a permission request before continuing. At the end, the selected image is attached in the editor and the user can continue generating or save the result. The user-perceived outcome is that a photo has been successfully added to the creation workspace. The system-level outcome is that the editor now contains the selected source image and is ready for image generation or modification.","steps":["Playground Editor","Source Image Options","Camera Permission","Photo Library Picker","Editor With Image Added"],"app":{"id":293,"name":"Apple Image Playground","description":"Create Fun Images Easily","background_url":"https://images.refero.design/backgrounds/app_293/4fb60cda-1c0a-4961-8bfb-a93734f5e4ca.jpg","refero_url":"https://refero.design/apps/293","categories":["AI Tool","Design & Media Editing"],"icon_url":"https://images.refero.design/favicon/app_293/1c5baa85-fc75-465e-9338-4a2800258ebd.jpg","background_color":"ec89ba"}},{"id":7989,"platform":"ios","screens_count":43,"refero_url":"https://refero.design/flows/7989","name":"Create suggested journal entry with media & location","description":"Happy-path: user opens the Timeline, creates a new journal entry using a suggested prompt, optionally enables Journaling Suggestions and push notifications, attaches media and a location, saves the entry and returns to the Timeline. Entry point is the Timeline; exit is the saved entry shown in Timeline. Assumptions: user is on a mobile device, already signed in, and the app can present system permission dialogs (notifications, location).","problem":"User task: create a new journal entry quickly using a curated suggestion and enrich it with media and a location.
- User perspective: start from Today in Timeline, pick a suggested prompt, write or paste text, add photos/audio and a location, and save. The user expects helpful suggestions, clear privacy cues, and straightforward permission prompts for notifications and location.
- Interface perspective: the UI exposes a Timeline card to open the editor, an editor with suggestion/scan/guided chips, an onboarding modal for Journaling Suggestions, system permission dialogs (notifications, location), a Suggestions browser (recommended/recent) with selectable prompt cards, and media/location pickers with search and map. The system shows privacy messaging before granting app-level access to suggested moment items.
Resulting outcome:
- User-perceived outcome: the journal entry is created with the chosen prompt, added media and location, and appears on the Timeline with tags (emotion, location, media). A confirmation (Saved now) appears.
- System-level outcome: the app may store the new entry and the selected media/location metadata; system permission choices (notifications/location) are persisted by the OS according to the user's selection.","steps":["Timeline (Today)","Entry editor (toolbar visible)","Empty editor state","Journaling Suggestions intro","Get suggestion notifications prompt","System notification permission","Suggestions browser (Private access alert)","Suggestions list (recommended cards)","Select suggestion (card expands)","Prompt detail / editable template","Add media entry point","System location permission request","Map preview / Change location","Location search input","Search returned no results","Search results shown","Location added to entry","Compose and save entry","Timeline updated (new card)","Final confirmation / entry state"],"app":{"id":229,"name":"ABY Journal","description":"Private Diary, Voice Journal","background_url":"https://images.refero.design/backgrounds/app_229/343870cc-9f56-43d6-81a4-154b8348717a.jpg","refero_url":"https://refero.design/apps/229","categories":["Health & Wellness","AI Tool","Lifestyle"],"icon_url":"https://images.refero.design/favicon/app_229/57d6e61f-5bd6-4b4b-8eec-dd68f5b5d7c9.jpg","background_color":"2fafee"}},{"id":8407,"platform":"ios","screens_count":5,"refero_url":"https://refero.design/flows/8407","name":"Add activity photos","description":"Happy-path for adding photos to an existing activity's details. Entry point: user is on an activity "Edit details" screen (logged in, has permission to edit). User opens the Photos picker, selects multiple images, confirms selection, and returns to the Edit details screen where thumbnails (including a cover photo) are displayed. Exit point: Edit details screen updated with the chosen photos. Assumptions: user is authenticated, has an existing activity to edit, device has access to the photo library, and the app can present a modal photo picker.","problem":"Task: Add photos to an activity (and implicitly choose a cover photo) so the activity has visual content when saved.

User perspective: The user wants to attach memorable photos to their run — they expect to open a photo selection interface, pick one or more images (with clear visual selection state and a count of chosen items), confirm the selection, and see the images added to the activity details (with one image shown as the cover). The user expects the flow to be reversible (cancel) and to return them to the same edit screen after confirming.

Interface/system perspective: The UI exposes an 'Add Photos' control on the Edit details screen that opens a modal photo picker. The photo picker shows a grid of available images with circular selection affordances. Selecting an image toggles a checked state and increments a selection count; the bottom of the modal exposes a 'Show Selected (n)' affordance while the top controls allow Cancel or Done. When the user confirms (Done), the system closes the picker, adds the selected photos to the activity, and displays thumbnails on the Edit details screen. The system-level result is that the activity record is updated with references to the newly attached images (and the UI marks one as a cover photo). The user-perceived outcome is the photos are visible in the activity details and one is labeled as the cover photo.","steps":["Edit details — Photos section","Photo picker — Grid view","Photo picker — Make selections","Confirm selection and return","Edit details — Photos updated"],"app":{"id":234,"name":"komoot","description":"Your all-in-one route planner","background_url":"https://images.refero.design/backgrounds/app_234/9d8562a9-a2a1-4fee-89dd-f05e15427178.jpg","refero_url":"https://refero.design/apps/234","categories":["Health & Wellness","Map & Navigation","Travel & Booking"],"icon_url":"https://images.refero.design/favicon/app_234/905598f0-aed1-497a-807b-05c35c43e228.jpg","background_color":"b7b715"}}]}
